name: Evening primrose oil
short: In trials, adverse effects were fairly common but mild, transient and mainly gastrointestinal, as with placebo. One study suggested it may increase bleeding in people taking warfarin.
text: A Cochrane review of 27 trials of oral evening primrose oil (19 trials) and borage oil (8 trials) for eczema found that both oils had the same fairly common, mild, transient adverse effects as the placebos, mainly gastrointestinal. The trials were short-term and did not examine long-term use: the review noted a case report warning of a potential risk of inflammation, thrombosis and immunosuppression when evening primrose oil is taken for more than one year, and another study which found it may increase bleeding in people taking warfarin. A clinical review described evening primrose oil as generally well tolerated, with minor adverse effects including gastrointestinal upset and headaches, and stated that its use during pregnancy is not supported in the literature and should be avoided.
